step0.title: Project & Simulation Setup
step0.subtitle: Configure project identity, simulation grid, and numerical settings.
step0.outputPrefixError: Alphanumeric and underscore only, max 20 chars
step0.outputPrefixTooltip:
Prefix for the output files and folders.

Affects: naming of all output files.
step0.cellSizeTooltip:
Cell size in metres. Smaller values increase accuracy but quadratically increase computation time (~x4 per halving).

Affects: resolution, computation time, memory usage.
step0.phasesTooltip:
Single-phase: one material type. Multi-phase (3): P1 Solid, P2 Fine-solid, P3 Fluid with independent momentum equations.

Affects: material parameters, outputs, inter-phase interactions.
step0.ctopoTooltip:
When enabled, flow height is measured perpendicular to the slope (slope-normal). When disabled, height is measured vertically. Slope-normal mode is better for steep terrain.

Affects: height interpretation in computations.
step0.limiterTooltip:
TVD flux limiter: Minmod (stable), Superbee (sharp fronts), Woodward, Van Leer.

Affects: numerical diffusion of flow fronts.
step0.gravityTooltip:
Gravitational acceleration. Earth = 9.81 m/s².

Affects: all forces — velocity, runout, pressure, energy.
step0.coresTooltip:
Number of CPU cores for parallel Monte Carlo runs.

Affects: parallelization of multiple runs only.
step0.thresholdsGroupTooltip:
Thresholds control which cells are displayed and which are considered 'active' in computation.

Affects: visual output, active cell detection, numerical stability.
step0.threshDisplayTooltip:
Minimum flow height threshold for display (metres). Cells below this are not shown.

Affects: visible cells. Lower = more detail + noise.
step0.threshKETooltip:
Kinetic energy threshold (J). Used for output filtering.

Affects: kinetic energy map filtering.
step0.threshPressureTooltip:
Pressure threshold (Pa). Used for output filtering.

Affects: pressure map filtering.
step0.threshHeightTooltip:
Height for velocity display (m).

Affects: velocity maps.
step0.threshVelocityTooltip:
Numerical threshold (m). Below this height a cell is considered dry. Critical for stability.

Affects: stability, active cell detection.
step0.cflGroupTooltip:
CFL criterion controls adaptive time stepping. CFL > 0.5 causes numerical instability.

Affects: time step size, numerical stability.
step0.cflNumberTooltip:
Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy number (0.01–0.5). Lower = more stable but slower. Max 0.5 is critical.

Affects: time step, stability.
step0.cflTimestepTooltip:
Fixed alternative timestep (s). When > 0, overrides CFL-based adaptive timestep.

Affects: time stepping method.
step0.slomoGroupTooltip:
Time scaling for slow geological processes. 1 = real time, 60 = minutes, 3600 = hours.

Affects: temporal scale of the simulation.
step0.slomoTimeTooltip:
Time scaling factor. 1 = real time. 60 = minutes, 3600 = hours, 86400 = days. Negative = geological.

Affects: temporal scale for slow processes.
step0.slomoViscosityTooltip:
Viscosity scaling for slow-motion mode. 1.0 = no change.

Affects: viscosity in slow-motion simulations.
step0.slomoFluxTooltip:
Flux scaling for slow-motion mode. 1.0 = no change.

Affects: mass flux in slow-motion simulations.
step0.multipleRunsGroupTooltip:
Monte Carlo mode runs the simulation multiple times with varied parameters for uncertainty analysis.

Affects: single vs ensemble mode.
step0.flagMTooltip:
Enable Monte Carlo multiple model runs with parameter sampling.

Affects: single vs ensemble mode.
step0.samplingTooltip:
Number of random parameter samples (+N), controlled (0), or OAT sensitivity (-N).

Affects: MC run count and method.
step0.aoiGroupTooltip:
Restrict computation to a sub-region of the DEM. Leave empty for full extent.

Affects: computation domain.
step0.aoiTooltip:
Area of interest coordinate (N/S/W/E) to restrict computation domain. Leave empty to use full DEM extent.

Affects: computation domain.

step1.title: Terrain & Release
step1.subtitle: Upload rasters and configure elevation, release heights, velocities, and hydrographs.
step1.uploadHint: Supports GeoTIFF (.tif, .tiff) and ASCII Grid (.asc) formats
step1.elevationTooltip:
Input DEM raster. In the release area, elevation = bottom of flow. Required.

Affects: all topographic computations.
step1.releaseHeightsGroupTooltip:
Define initial release volumes per phase. Non-zero cells define the release area.

Affects: initial flow volume and release location.
step1.rhrelease1Tooltip:
Fractional ratio (0–1) of P1 release height relative to total. Required when using hrelease with phases=3.

Affects: phase partitioning of release.
step1.vhreleaseTooltip:
Randomization bounds (min,max) for release height. Only used in Monte Carlo mode.

Affects: MC height variation.
step1.releaseTimeGroupTooltip:
Control when material is released at each cell. Optional for delayed or continuous sources.

Affects: temporal sequence of release.
step1.initialVelocityGroupTooltip:
Set initial velocity rasters per phase. X = east-west (positive = east), Y = north-south (positive = north).

Affects: initial momentum.
step1.hydrographGroupTooltip:
Time-varying inflow boundary. Requires both a hydrograph file and coordinates.

Affects: mass inflow over time.
step1.hreleaseTooltip:
Raster map defining initial release height (metres). Non-zero cells = release area.

Affects: initial volume and release location.
step1.treleaseTooltip:
Raster map of time delay (seconds) before release starts at each cell.

Affects: temporal sequence.
step1.trelstopTooltip:
Raster map of time (seconds) when release stops. For continuous sources.

Affects: source duration.
step1.velocityTooltip:
Raster map of initial velocity (m/s). X = east-west, Y = north-south.

Affects: initial momentum.
step1.hydrographTooltip:
Path to text file with time-varying inflow (time, discharge pairs).

Affects: mass inflow over time.
step1.hydrocoordsTooltip:
Coordinates: x, y, cross-section length, flow direction (degrees).

Affects: inflow location.
step1.validationError: At least one release height (P1, P2, or P3) must be selected.

step2.title: Material Properties
step2.subtitle: Define physical parameters for each phase: density, friction, cohesion, viscosity, and deformation.
step2.densityTooltip:
Mass density per phase (kg/m³). P1: grain density of solid (2700 rock). P2: fine-solid mixture (1850). P3: fluid (1000 water).

Affects: flow velocity, momentum, runout distance, deposit thickness.
step2.frictionTooltip:
Internal, basal, and fluid friction angles per phase. Internal > basal typically. Fluid friction for turbulent effects.

Affects: flow velocity, runout distance, lateral spreading.
step2.cohesionTooltip:
Cohesive strength per phase (N/m²). Resistance independent of normal stress. 0 = non-cohesive granular.

Affects: flow initiation, deposit stability.
step2.viscosityTooltip:
Log10 of kinematic viscosity per phase (m²/s). E.g. -7 = 10^-7. Controls fluid-like behaviour.

Affects: flow spreading, velocity profile.
step2.deformationTooltip:
Deformation coefficient (0–1) per phase. 1 = fully deformable, 0 = rigid block.

Affects: material deformation during flow.
step2.clayersTooltip:
Layer mode: solid phase forms a basal layer beneath the fluid phase.

Affects: vertical structure of the flow.
step2.cdispersionTooltip:
Lateral pressure spreading. 0=off, 1–3=progressive dispersion levels.

Affects: lateral flow spreading.
step2.csurfaceTooltip:
Surface control for reservoir/lake: 0=off, 1=edges, 2=within, 3=both.

Affects: water surface balancing.
step2.dragGroupTooltip:
Inter-phase drag parameters controlling momentum exchange between solid, fine-solid, and fluid phases.

Affects: phase coupling, velocity differences between phases.
step2.drag0Tooltip:
KDrag (m/s). Controls inter-phase momentum exchange rate.

Affects: phase coupling strength.
step2.drag1Tooltip:
Exponent mDrag. Controls drag dependence on concentration.

Affects: drag scaling with phase fraction.
step2.drag2Tooltip:
Drag type nDrag. Selects the drag model formulation.

Affects: drag model behaviour.
step2.dragUtTooltip:
Terminal velocity Ut (m/s). Settling velocity of solid particles.

Affects: phase separation rate.
step2.dragRepTooltip:
Particle Reynolds number Rep.

Affects: drag coefficient calculation.
step2.dragJTooltip:
Exponent j. Stokes = 3 for fine particles.

Affects: drag force scaling.
step2.virtualMassGroupTooltip:
Virtual mass accounts for the added inertia of accelerating one phase relative to another.

Affects: phase acceleration coupling.
step2.vm0Tooltip:
Virtual mass number Nvm.

Affects: virtual mass contribution.
step2.vm1Tooltip:
Virtual mass coefficient lvm.

Affects: virtual mass strength.
step2.vm2Tooltip:
Virtual mass control nvm.

Affects: virtual mass model.
step2.slideparGroupTooltip:
Sliding parameters control block-like vs deformable motion. Exponents (0–2) and fractions (0–1) per phase.

Affects: flow regime (block vs deformable).
step2.slideparTooltip:
Sliding exponent (0–2) and fraction (0–1) per phase. 0 = fully deformable.

Affects: flow regime.
step2.shearingTooltip:
Energy dissipation through internal shearing.

Affects: energy losses within flow mass.
step2.ambientTooltip:
Ambient (air) drag coefficient. 0 = no air resistance.

Affects: flow deceleration from air drag.
step2.fragmentationTooltip:
Rock breakup parameters. 0 = no fragmentation.

Affects: material disintegration during flow.
step2.spatialOverridesGroupTooltip:
Raster maps that override scalar parameters spatially. Each cell gets its own value.

Affects: spatial variation of friction, cohesion, viscosity, etc.
step2.frictiographTooltip:
Path to text file with time-varying friction changes.

Affects: friction evolution over time.

step3.title: Entrainment, Stopping & Phase Transformation
step3.subtitle: Configure erosion, deposition, stopping criteria, and phase transformations.
step3.entrainmentCoeffTooltip: LOG10 of the entrainment coefficient. E.g. -7.0 means 10^-7. More negative = less entrainment.
step3.entrainmentGroupTooltip:
Entrainment: flow erodes and incorporates underlying material as it moves.

Affects: total flow volume, runout distance, deposit depth.
step3.centrainmentTooltip:
When enabled, the flow erodes and incorporates underlying material using a momentum-based approach.

Affects: erosion, flow volume growth.
step3.stoppingThresholdTooltip:
Threshold for selected stopping criterion. Flow deposits when criterion drops below this.

Affects: deposition timing.
step3.hentrmaxTooltip:
Raster map of maximum entrainment depth (metres) per phase.

Affects: maximum erosion depth.
step3.rhentrmax1Tooltip:
Fractional ratio (0–1) of P1 entrainment relative to total. Required with hentrmax + phases=3.

Affects: phase partitioning of entrained material.
step3.vhentrmaxTooltip:
Randomization bounds (min,max) for entrainment height. Only in MC mode.

Affects: MC entrainment variation.
step3.centrTooltip:
Raster map of spatially variable entrainment coefficient (log10). Overrides scalar.

Affects: spatial entrainment pattern.
step3.stoppingGroupTooltip:
Stopping criterion determines when flow begins depositing material.

Affects: deposit extent and timing.
step3.cstoppingTooltip:
Stopping criterion: 0=off, 1=kinetic energy, 2=momentum, 3=dynamic pressure.

Affects: deposition onset.
step3.tstopTooltip:
Raster map of stopping time (seconds) per cell.

Affects: forced deposition timing.
step3.phaseTransformationGroupTooltip:
Phase transformation: material changes between solid, fine-solid, and fluid phases during flow.

Affects: phase composition evolution.
step3.cmeltTooltip:
Enable temperature-dependent ice melting and phase transformation.

Affects: solid-to-fluid transformation.
step3.transformationCoeffGroupTooltip:
Log10 of transformation coefficients between phase pairs. 0 = no transformation.

Affects: phase transformation rates.
step3.trans12Tooltip:
Log10 of P1→P2 transformation coefficient. 0 = none.

Affects: solid to fine-solid conversion.
step3.trans13Tooltip:
Log10 of P1→P3 transformation coefficient. 0 = none.

Affects: solid to fluid conversion.
step3.trans23Tooltip:
Log10 of P2→P3 transformation coefficient. 0 = none.

Affects: fine-solid to fluid conversion.
step3.meltingGroupTooltip:
Temperature and melting parameters for ice/snow melting during flow.

Affects: phase transformation driven by temperature.
step3.tLandslideTooltip:
Initial temperature of landslide material (°C).

Affects: melting rate calculation.
step3.tGroundTooltip:
Ground surface temperature (°C).

Affects: basal melting rate.
step3.meltEfficiencyTooltip:
Melt efficiency (0–1). Fraction of heat energy that causes melting.

Affects: melting rate.
step3.slideFractionTooltip:
Sliding fraction (0–1). Fraction of basal motion contributing to heat.

Affects: frictional heating.
step3.transformRastersGroupTooltip:
Raster maps for spatially variable phase transformation coefficients.

Affects: spatial transformation pattern.
step3.transformographTooltip:
Path to text file with time-varying transformation coefficients.

Affects: transformation evolution over time.

step4.title: Output & Timing
step4.subtitle: Configure simulation time, output flags, and reference data.
step4.outputIntervalTooltip:
Time interval between saved output snapshots (seconds).

Affects: output file count, disk usage.
step4.endTimeTooltip:
Total simulation end time (seconds). Must be greater than output interval.

Affects: total simulation duration.
step4.endTimeValidation: End time must be greater than output interval.
step4.outputFlagsGroupTooltip:
Control what types of output are generated. More flags = more disk usage.

Affects: output types and disk usage.
step4.flagVTooltip:
Generate R-based visualization plots, maps, and animations.

Affects: visual outputs (requires R).
step4.flagKTooltip:
Keep intermediate GRASS GIS raster maps after simulation.

Affects: disk usage, enables custom post-processing.
step4.flagATooltip:
Generate velocity, pressure, and kinetic energy rasters per timestep.

Affects: additional output rasters.
step4.flagTTooltip:
Generate tsunami height raster maps per timestep.

Affects: tsunami-related outputs.
step4.referenceDataGroupTooltip:
Observed data for validation: compare simulated results against field measurements.

Affects: AUROC, validation metrics.
step4.impactareaTooltip:
Observed impact area raster (binary 0/1) for validation.

Affects: AUROC and accuracy metrics.
step4.hdepositTooltip:
Observed deposit height raster (m) for validation.

Affects: simulated vs observed comparison.
step4.zonesTooltip:
Zone classification raster for spatially differentiated analysis.

Affects: zonal statistics of results.
step4.profileTooltip:
Profile line coordinates (x1,y1,x2,y2,...) for cross-section extraction.

Affects: profile data in results.
step4.ctrlpointsTooltip:
Control point coordinates (x1,y1,x2,y2,...) for time series extraction.

Affects: time series at specific locations.

step5.title: Visualization
step5.subtitle: Configure orthophoto overlay and display parameters. All settings are optional.
step5.orthophotoGroupTooltip:
RGB channels for background orthophoto overlay in visualizations.

Affects: map background in output plots.
step5.displayParamsGroupTooltip:
Control how flow, contours, and colors are displayed in the visualization output.

Affects: visual appearance of all output maps.
step5.vizDeformTooltip:
Show orthophoto deformation: 0=none, 1=with flow destruction.

Affects: terrain visualization.
step5.hflowminTooltip:
Minimum flow height displayed (m). Below this, flow is invisible.

Affects: visual sensitivity.
step5.hflowrefTooltip:
Reference flow height (m) for color scaling. Higher = more saturated.

Affects: color mapping of flow depth.
step5.htsunrefTooltip:
Reference tsunami height (m) for color scaling.

Affects: tsunami visualization.
step5.hcontminTooltip:
Minimum flow contour level (m).

Affects: contour line range.
step5.hcontmaxTooltip:
Maximum flow contour level (m).

Affects: contour line range.
step5.hcontintTooltip:
Flow contour interval (m).

Affects: contour line density.
step5.zcontminTooltip:
Minimum elevation contour (m).

Affects: terrain contour range.
step5.zcontmaxTooltip:
Maximum elevation contour (m).

Affects: terrain contour range.
step5.zcontintTooltip:
Elevation contour interval (m).

Affects: terrain contour density.
step5.predTooltip:
Red color weight (0–1) in flow visualization.

Affects: flow color appearance.
step5.pgreenTooltip:
Green color weight (0–1) in flow visualization.

Affects: flow color appearance.
step5.pblueTooltip:
Blue color weight (0–1) in flow visualization.

Affects: flow color appearance.
step5.pexpTooltip:
Transparency exponent for flow overlay.

Affects: flow transparency.
step5.phexaggTooltip:
Profile height exaggeration factor.

Affects: vertical scale in profile plots.
step5.pvpathTooltip:
Path to ParaView pvpython executable.

Affects: 3D visualization availability.
step5.rscriptpathTooltip:
Path to Rscript executable.

avaflow.title: About r.avaflow
avaflow.subtitle: Open-source mass flow simulation tool
avaflow.overviewP1: r.avaflow is an open-source, GIS-based simulation framework for the propagation of rapid mass flows. It operates as a raster module within GRASS GIS and supports the modeling of complex, multi-phase geophysical processes including avalanches, debris flows, lahars, landslides, rock-ice avalanches, and tsunamis.
avaflow.overviewP2: The underlying physics engine is based on the Pudasaini & Mergili multi-phase mass flow model, which describes the dynamics of a mixture of solid, fine-solid, and fluid phases flowing over general topography.
avaflow.authorsLeadDevValue: Martin Mergili — University of Graz, Austria
avaflow.authorsPhysModelValue: Shiva P. Pudasaini — University of Bonn, Germany
avaflow.cap1Desc: Two- and three-phase system: solid, fine-solid, and fluid components with independent momentum equations.
avaflow.cap2Desc: Dynamic basal erosion and incorporation of bed material into the flowing mass.
avaflow.cap3Desc: Conversion between solid and fluid phases driven by excess pore pressure and shear.
avaflow.cap4Desc: Physically-based criteria for progressive deposition and complete stopping of the flow.
avaflow.cap5Desc: Simulation of cascading processes such as landslide-triggered tsunamis or dam-break floods.
avaflow.cap6Desc: Native raster module leveraging GRASS GIS for spatial data management and visualization.
avaflow.ref1: Mergili, M., Pudasaini, S.P. (2020–2023). r.avaflow — The mass flow simulation tool. r.avaflow 3 (20230127).
avaflow.ref2: Pudasaini, S.P., Mergili, M. (2019). A multi-phase mass flow model. Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface, 124, 2920–2942.
avaflow.ref3: Mergili, M., Fischer, J.-T., Krenn, J., Pudasaini, S.P. (2017). r.avaflow v1, an advanced open-source computational framework for the propagation and interaction of two-phase mass flows. Geoscientific Model Development, 10, 553–569.

app.title: About this app
app.subtitle: r.avaflow Web App
app.overviewText: The r.avaflow Web App provides a modern browser-based interface for configuring, executing, and analyzing r.avaflow simulations. It replaces the traditional command-line workflow with a guided, visual experience.
app.feat1Desc: Create, open, save, and delete simulation projects from the sidebar.
app.feat2Desc: Guided configuration: general settings, release parameters, materials, numerics, and output options.
app.feat3Desc: Live log streaming and progress tracking via WebSocket connection.
app.feat4Desc: Explore simulation outputs, review logs, and access generated raster files.
app.feat5Desc: Simulations run inside isolated Docker containers with GRASS GIS pre-installed.
app.feat6Desc: Toggle between light and dark modes using the sidebar theme switcher.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.subtitle: Quick start guide, parameter reference & FAQ
docs.step1Desc: Click "New project" in the sidebar or open an existing project from the project list.
docs.step2Desc: In Step 1 of the wizard, provide the DEM (digital elevation model) and release height raster files. Optionally add entrainment, friction, and other spatial input layers.
docs.step3Desc: Walk through Steps 2–5 of the wizard: set phase properties, material parameters, numerical controls, and output preferences.
docs.step4Desc: Click "Run" at the final wizard step or use the play button next to the project name. The simulation executes inside a Docker container.
docs.step5Desc: Switch to the Modeling tab to watch live logs. Once finished, open the Results tab to inspect outputs.
docs.paramPhasesDesc: Phase model: s (solid), fs (fine-solid), f (fluid), or combinations. Use 3 for the 40G version.
docs.paramCellsizeDesc: Raster cell size in meters. Smaller values increase resolution and computation time.
docs.paramTintDesc: Time interval: output interval (s) and total simulation time (s), comma-separated.
docs.paramDensityDesc: Phase densities (kg/m³) for solid, fine-solid, and fluid.
docs.paramFrictionDesc: Basal friction angles (degrees) for solid, fine-solid, and fluid.
docs.paramElevationDesc: Input DEM raster (required). Defines the topographic surface.
docs.paramHreleaseDesc: Release height raster. Cells with value > 0 define the initial mass source.
docs.paramCflDesc: CFL (Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy) number controlling time step stability.
docs.paramThresholdsDesc: Flow depth thresholds for visualization and stopping criteria.
docs.paramFullListHint: See the full parameter list in the official r.avaflow documentation.
docs.faq1Answer: Ensure Docker is installed and running on the server. The backend needs access to the Docker socket to create containers. On Linux, the user running the NestJS server must be in the docker group.
docs.faq2Answer: The project directory exists but lacks a .json configuration file. This usually means the project was created by a script run, not through the wizard. You can still run these projects using the play button, but cannot edit them in the Parameters tab.
docs.faq3Title: Simulation runs but produces no output
docs.faq3Answer: Check that the release height raster (hrelease) has non-zero values and spatially overlaps the DEM. Also verify that the time interval is long enough for the flow to propagate.
docs.faq4Answer: Results appear only after a simulation completes. Switch to the Modeling tab to check if the simulation is still running or if it encountered an error.
docs.faq5Title: How do I use the three-phase model?
docs.faq5Answer: Set phases to s,fs,f (or 3 for the 40G version). You will need to provide density and friction values for all three phases. The three-phase model is significantly more computationally expensive.
docs.faq6Title: Can I run multiple simulations simultaneously?
docs.faq6Answer: Yes. Each simulation runs in its own Docker container. However, be mindful of available CPU and memory resources on the server.
